title: iMOD Coupler product integration
findings: Upstream DriverType currently contains metamod, ribamod and ribametamod only.
Upstream get_driver is a hard-coded product registry and exposes no external entry-point/plugin mechanism.
The actual MetaMod driver owns the coupled timestep lifecycle; F-GC50 must integrate at this product layer rather than duplicate it inside SWAP5.
F-GC49D Python runtime consumes a positive pre-existing opaque Fortran context handle.
F-GC49D production C ABI does not construct an application context from product configuration.
The F-GC49D fixture can create a test context but remains qualification-only and is ineligible for product bootstrap.
F-GC50 must reuse an admitted application/bootstrap owner, potentially the active M1-C3/F-APP line or another separately admitted typed bootstrap.

blockers.description: Actual iMOD Coupler product registration requires an upstream source change, but the connected repository permission is read/pull only.

No admitted production C/Python bootstrap currently creates the F-GC49D Fortran application context from product configuration; F-GC50 may not promote a qualification fixture or invent a second state owner.

exclusions: Python ownership of SWAP/FMR state or ledgers

qualification.workflow: F-GC50 iMOD Coupler product integration reconcile

next_permitted_action: Resume product integration only when BOTH prerequisites exist: (1) a real authorized iMOD Coupler product mutation/extension route that can register the SWAP5 driver in the upstream product lifecycle, and (2) an admitted SWAP5 production application bootstrap that creates/owns the F-GC49D context without qualification fixtures or Python-owned SWAP state. Until then, do not implement a local get_driver imitation, monkeypatch, duplicate coupling loop, or F-GC49 Stage E.

canonical_reconciliation.disposition: Post-qualification canonical drift is the admitted documentation-authority refresh only. The F-GC50 upstream contract test, runner, workflow and integration contract are transplanted byte-identically; qualification evidence remains valid.
